newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Three arrested in raids in Antwerp diamond quarter.
newsitem.headline: Three arrested in raids in Antwerp diamond quarter.

text.p: Belgian police have arrested three men from the Antwerp diamond scene on charges of having laundered an estimated $28 million through two small local banks, the Antwerp public prosecutor's office said on Tuesday.
The men, who were not named, were put in police custody after raids on Monday and also charged with fraud, tax evasion and culpable bankruptcy, spokeswoman Leen Nuyts told Reuters.

The arrests were part of an investigation into the bankruptcy of Antwerp Bank Max Fischer in January of this year and the use of false accounts. Nuyts said there had been other arrests in the Fischer case, but could not give details.
She declined to name the banks involved.
Two of those arrested on Monday are brothers -- one of them the manager of the banks and both active in the financing of the diamond trade.
Belgian media said authorities sealed a vault holding more than one billion Belgian francs ($28 million) worth of diamonds and several hundred thousand francs of cash in the operation.

Marc Van den Abeelen, general manager of the industry body Diamond High Council, said the three men "had abused the diamond scene" and noted the raids were bad for the reputation of Antwerp as a diamond trading centre.
Noting this was the third investigation into Antwerp's diamond sector, he told Belgian radio, "It is the job of the judiciary to clear things up."
The sector has annual turnover of 600 billion francs ($16.8 million) and employs 30,000 in Antwerp.
